definitions.explanation: Completely wet through, typically from rain or immersion in water.

examples.japanese: {雨|あめ}でずぶ{濡|ぬ}れになった。
examples.english: I got soaking wet from the rain.

examples.japanese: {傘|かさ}を{忘|わす}れて、ずぶ{濡|ぬ}れで{帰|かえ}ってきた。
examples.english: I forgot my umbrella and came home soaking wet.

examples.japanese: ずぶ{濡|ぬ}れの{服|ふく}を{着替|きが}えた。
examples.english: I changed out of my soaking wet clothes.

notes:
USAGE: ずぶ{濡|ぬ}れ emphasizes being completely soaked through, more extreme than just being wet.

GRAMMAR:
・As a noun: ずぶ{濡|ぬ}れの＋noun (soaking wet ~)
・With なる: ずぶ{濡|ぬ}れになる (to become soaking wet)
・With で: ずぶ{濡|ぬ}れで＋verb (do something while soaking wet)

COMMON PATTERNS:
・ずぶ{濡|ぬ}れになる (to get drenched)
・ずぶ{濡|ぬ}れの{状態|じょうたい} (drenched state)

NUANCE: The prefix ずぶ is an intensifier meaning "completely" or "thoroughly," similar to びしょ in びしょ{濡|ぬ}れ.

RELATED:
・びしょ{濡|ぬ}れ - sopping wet (similar intensity)
・{濡|ぬ}れる - to get wet (verb)
